body:
Pass 18. Verified the crossnobis slice - correctness is exact: package 0.329503620772 vs base-R oracle 0.329503620772, max|diff| 5.55e-17.

More importantly your Monte Carlo test has real power. I replicated test-crossnobis-known.R:275 in base R and pushed a deliberately non-crossvalidated estimator through it: null mean +0.09791 vs se 0.00611, i.e. 16.03 se - your 4-se gate catches it. The correct estimator sits at 0.63 se (null) and 0.25 se (signal). That closes the "zero parameter-recovery tests" finding from the original review.

One refinement while the epic is open: the tolerance is 4 * sd(estimates)/sqrt(replications), computed from the observed data, but your acceptance says PRESPECIFIED. An adaptive gate widens with the noise, so a defect that inflates variance without biasing the mean would pass. Measured expected se in your config at 120 reps: ~0.0058 null, ~0.0119 signal. Pin them, keep the 4-sigma mean gates, and bound the observed se (1.5x expected). Then it fails for bias and for variance inflation.

Also worth documenting explicitly that the /features per-channel normalization is a deliberate convention - it differs from an unnormalized squared Mahalanobis and users will assume one or the other.
